newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hutchison shares dip in favour of parent.
newsitem.headline: Hutchison shares dip in favour of parent.

text.p: Hutchison Whampoa Ltd shares lost ground on Wednesday as those of Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd rose, in what analysts and traders said could be the start of a shift out of Hutchison and into parent Cheung Kong.
"There is a good arbitrage opportunity here," said a trader with a U.S. house.
Hutchison Whampoa lost HK$0.75 to HK$60.50 on moderately heavy trade worth HK$344.38 million, while Cheung Kong leaped HK$2.00 to HK$74.75 on very heavy turnover of HK$711.54 million.
The other two listed members of the group also had mixed fortunes on Wednesday.
Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd rose HK$0.50 to HK$21.75, while Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd fell HK$0.50 to HK$27.15 after surging HK$2.40 on Tuesday.

Hutchison Whampoa, the diversified conglomerate within the Cheung Kong group, has been an overseas institutional portfolio favourite and has traded on a price-earnings ratio (PER) of nearly twice that of its parent.
Based on Wednesday's closing price, Hutchison is trading on a PER of 23.11 times historic earnings, while Cheung Kong is rated 14.38 times after its strong surge of the past two days.

While the restructuring of the Cheung Kong group, which eventually will give Cheung Kong a 50 percent or greater holding in Hutchison, may be one reason for the difference in trading patterns, analysts pointed out that all property developers saw good gains on Wednesday.
"Cheung Kong is cheap on a PER basis," said Percy Au-Yeung, director of research at DBS Securities.
"And the outlook is sweetened by the exceptional gains (on the sale of its Cheung Kong Infrastructure stake), but all the developers did well today."

The property sector led the market on Wednesday, boosted chiefly by the gains in Cheung Kong. Henderson Land rose HK$1.25 to HK$76.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties added HK$1.00 to HK$95.25. New World Development was unchanged at HK$53.75.

"Stripping out the Hutchison stake, Cheung Kong's property assets are trading at a 40 percent discount to their NAV (net asset value)," said Mark Simpson, director of Hong Kong research at ING Barings.
He added that the discount was significantly greater than for other property shares.
